title: Console launch: sculpting dashboard + tracing + cost breakdown surface for MVP
creator: Morgan Lee
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures a targeted scope reduction and acceptance criteria for the Redwood Console launch surface: dashboards, tracing, and per-route cost breakdown. We need a focused MVP that surfaces high-value signals for product and infra teams while deferring lower-value polishing work. The goal is to remove ambiguity, document decisions, and provide devs with a narrow, testable scope for the next two sprints.

Background:
- Multiple stakeholders asked for a broad set of telemetry views in time for launch. Implementation velocity is slower than expected and dependencies (instrumentation, aggregator, sampling policy) risk delaying GA.
- We must preserve core user outcomes: (1) quickly identify high-latency routes, (2) attribute cost to model routes and deployments, (3) get sample traces with token-level span timing for debugging.

Proposed MVP cuts / scope sculpting (what we will implement for launch):
1) Dashboards: deliver two dashboard tiles only - Route Health (latency + error rate top 10) and Cost Trend (total token spend by route, 30d). Defer per-tenant drilldown and custom tile builder.
2) Tracing: provide sampled end-to-end traces with key spans (client->gateway, runtime queue, model inference). Defer full waterfall UI and timeline zooming; provide downloadable trace JSON for deeper analysis.
3) Cost breakdown: implement per-route token accounting and simple cost attribution using model/variant tags. Defer allocation rules, cross-customer chargebacks, and cost forecasting.
4) Rollouts & fallback surface: build basic rollout status card (active/canary/fallback) with last 24h success rate. Defer A/B cohort analysis and rollout comparison charts.
5) Alerting & SLOs: include baked-in SLO targets in UI for the top two routes only; defer multi-SLO dashboards and custom alert creation.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Narrowing dashboards eliminates early requests for customization but ensures core signals are available at GA.
- Shipping sampled traces without a full waterfall reduces UX work and allows engineers to iterate on trace parsing tooling first.
- Cost attribution via tags is quick to implement and buys time for a richer allocation model later.

Non-goals for launch (explicitly out):
- Per-tenant custom dashboards, graph builder, historical anomaly detection, per-token flamegraphs, chargeback exports, scheduled reports, RBAC-per-dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Route Health tile shows top 10 routes by p95 latency and error rate; data refresh <=60s
Cost Trend tile displays 30-day total token spend per route, with ability to filter by model tag
Traces are stored for sampled requests (default 0.5% sampling) and contain the required spans: gateway, runtime-queue, model-infer. Export link to trace JSON present on trace detail page
Rollout status card reflects current route rollout state and last 24h success rate; toggling between routes works for routes with >1000 requests/day
SLO card displays configured p95 latency target and current burn rate for the two target routes
End-to-end smoke test passes: dashboard tiles populate from staging telemetry within 60s of synthetic traffic; trace export contains token-count metadata
Performance: dashboard queries do not increase tail latency of the serving runtime by >5% in staging under baseline load
Docs: PRD + short explainer doc for deferred features (list and rationale) published in Confluence and linked from the UI help
decisions: Keep sampling low (0.5%) to control storage and UI load for GA; adjust via feature flag post-launch
Prioritize per-route token accounting over full allocation rules to deliver cost visibility quickly
Expose trace JSON export instead of full waterfall UI to reduce front-end scope
Limit dashboard tiles to two canonical views to reduce instrumentation and query complexity
rollout_plan: Week 1 (2025-10-06 to 2025-10-10): finalize wireframes and data contracts; instrumentation owners sign-off
Week 2 (2025-10-13 to 2025-10-17): backend implementations (aggregator queries, cost tagging, trace capture); internal QA on staging
Week 3 (2025-10-20 to 2025-10-24): front-end tiles and trace viewer; docs and show-and-tell with support/SE
Canary (2025-10-27): enable for 10% of production traffic for three high-usage customers; monitor for regressions
GA (target 2025-11-03): enable UI for all customers; open follow-up tickets for deferred features
dependencies: ENG-89210 (tracing: add model-infer span and token-count metadata)
